title: Federal Rule 9 — pleading special matters
summary: Rule 9(b) requires particular circumstances for allegations of fraud or mistake. The requirement concerns the pleaded theory, not simply the title of the statute under which the party sues.

sections.Role in the course: Rule 9(b) requires particular circumstances for allegations of fraud or mistake. The requirement concerns the pleaded theory, not simply the title of the statute under which the party sues.
sections.What to examine: Identify the allegedly false statement or omission, the responsible actor, relevant time and setting, and how it figures in the claim. Kearns examines consumer claims founded on a course of alleged fraud. Check the rule’s different treatment of mental conditions and any additional statute.
